title: Senior's toolkit: loading and selecting with pandas
summary: read_csv options that prevent bad data, loc and iloc, query, assign, pipe and Parquet.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: loading and selecting with pandas
steps.body: Most pandas trouble starts at load time (wrong types, dates left as text) or with selection that edits a copy. These are the options experienced analysts set on purpose.

toolkit.what: Load a CSV with the right types from the start, instead of fixing them afterwards.
flags: load only these columns: faster, less memory
keep codes as text, so `00123` keeps its zeros
read a slice first to check the file

toolkit.what: Select by labels or a boolean mask, and assign through it. `iloc` selects by position.
flags: set a column on the matching rows, in one step
first five rows of the first column

toolkit.what: Filter with a readable expression. `@name` uses a Python variable.
flags: refer to a variable in your code
wrap a column name that has spaces in backticks

toolkit.what: Add columns and return a new frame, so steps chain. A lambda receives the frame as it is at that point.
flags: later ones can use earlier ones
toolkit.example: orders = orders.assign(total=lambda d: d.qty * d.price, big=lambda d: d.total > 100)

toolkit.what: Call your own function inside a method chain, so a cleaning pipeline reads top to bottom.
Save to Parquet: types are kept, files are small and fast to read. Needs `pyarrow` installed.
flags: do not store the row index

steps.prompt: Finance says product `00123` is missing from your report, but there is a product `123` nobody recognises. What went wrong at load time?
options: `read_csv` guessed the `sku` column was numeric and dropped the leading zeros; load it with `dtype={"sku": "string"}`
pandas sorts codes numerically and renamed it
steps.explain: Codes (SKUs, ZIP codes, phone numbers, account numbers) are text that happens to contain digits. Say so with `dtype`, or the type guess quietly changes them.

steps.prompt: This line runs, but `orders` still has no 20% VAT for UK rows (pandas 3, or pandas 2 with copy-on-write). Why, and what is the fix?
options: The filter makes a new frame and the assignment changes only that; use `orders.loc[orders["country"] == "UK", "vat"] = 0.2`
The column must exist before it can be assigned
steps.explain: This is chained assignment: two indexing steps, so the value lands in a temporary result. With copy-on-write it never changes `orders` (pandas warns about it). One `.loc[rows, col]` call updates the original.

steps.prompt: Load three columns, read `day` as dates, then keep orders above a limit stored in the variable `limit`.
steps.explain: `usecols` limits what is read, `parse_dates` turns text into datetimes, and `@` lets a query string refer to a Python variable.
The totals are 10, 10 and 6. `query` keeps the rows where the total is at least 10, and it keeps their original index labels 0 and 1.

steps.prompt: Match each call to its job.
pairs: the first five rows by position
add a column inside a chain
call your own function in a chain

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Give `read_csv` the types you know (`dtype`, `parse_dates`, `usecols`) instead of trusting its guesses, and save intermediate results as Parquet so the types survive. Assign through one `.loc[rows, col]`, and write transformations as a chain of `assign`, `query` and `pipe` that a reviewer can read top to bottom.
